content: Integer-key hasher landscape: FxHash is very fast but low quality (predictable, clustering-prone); rustc measured fnv->fxhash up to 6% faster but fxhash->ahash 1-4% SLOWER, i.e. ahash is already near-optimal for integer keys. rustc-hash 2.x changed algorithm (polynomial for ints, wyhash-inspired for bytes, MSRV 1.77). ahash passes SMHasher and is per-process randomly seeded; wyhash passes SMHasher/BigCrush; hashbrown >=0.15 defaults to foldhash. SwissTable uses top hash bits for control bytes and low bits for bucket index, so weak high-bit avalanche clusters probes; hashbrown README shows 4.2-6.75x swings between hashers on serial/high-bit-heavy keys. Hash quality also governs DashMap shard balance. Sources: Rust Performance Book hashing chapter, hashbrown README + bench suite, devgenius deep dive, rustc-hash overview.
